newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign investment in Poland $21 bln by 2000 - study.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Poland $21 bln by 2000 - study.

text.p: Overall foreign investment in Poland may reach $21-$22 billion by the year 2000 and is likely to remain a major factor in the country's economic growth, a study by the National Chamber of Commerce said.

A joint study by the Chamber and Gdansk University's economics department showed that foreign investment had been responsible for 38 percent of Polish GDP growth in 1991 to 1995, the Chamber's research director told Reuters on Monday.
Przemyslaw Kulawczyk said Poland had recently observed a clear growth trend in foreign investments.
"The forecast for this year alone is $4.2 billion," he said.

The study's projection for total foreign investment by 2000 was more cautious than that of the government's Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ), which forecast in late September that the figure would reach $30 billion.
PAIZ said total foreign direct investment, since Poland launched market reforms in 1990, was $4.3 billion in December 1994 and $6.8 billion in December 1995.
In July 1996 the figure reached $10.2 billion.
PAIZ forecast the investment inflow this year alone would be $4 billion.
Kulawczyk said Polish firms had quickly adopted the management style of Western rivals investing in Poland.
"After two to three years, Polish firms, mostly private or recently privatised, reached the same standard as Western firms coming here and are even better in various areas," he said.
